newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya police shoot dead Irish priest, church says.
newsitem.headline: Kenya police shoot dead Irish priest, church says.

text.p: Kenyan police have shot dead an Irish Roman Catholic priest after he confronted local officials over alleged corruption, a statement from central Nakuru diocese said on Saturday.

The statement titled "Senseless Killing of a Missionary" demanded an explanation for the shooting and three other violent robberies on Catholic missions this month. The statement was published in the Daily Nation leading newspaper.
It said the priest, Larry Timmons, died on Wednesday after being shot by Administration Police a day after confronting officials over bribery and discrimination surrounding new identity cards.

"The Catholic Diocese of Nakuru is utterly shocked and is in disbelief to note that the following day (Wednesday) Timmons died after being hit by bullets fired by the Administration Police," the statement said.
"We cannot help but relate the killing with the prior confrontation between our brother and the administration."
The East African Standard newspaper reported on Thursday that Timmons was shot dead by two police who intervened in an attempted robbery at his mission.
Nakuru police confirmed the shooting and said two officers were being questioned, the Standard added.
"It seems that this is yet another police killing in the country," opposition FORD-Kenya MP Paul Muite told reporters at a march on Saturday protesting human rights abuses in Kenya.

London-based human rights group Amnesty International said this month the Kenyan government has failed to halt widespread torture of men, women and children which involves electric shocks and sexual abuse -- a charge denied by the government.
Kenya's Anglican and Catholic churches called last year for constitutional change, a long-held position that has led to frequent rows with the government.
